_note: HAND-AUTHORED source for the book's ARGUMENT-SPINE model — the book's linear argument as an ordered run of numbered claims, plus the per-chapter labeling of which spine claims each chapter advances. This file IS edited by hand; argument-spine.json is generated from it (`python3 book-models/argument_spine_model.py regenerate`). Mirrors claims_declared.json's declared-source→generated-artifact shape. WHY A NEW MODEL, NOT AN EXTENSION: the claims model holds unordered stances with a contradiction predicate; the Big-Ideas model holds six fixed landing slots. A spine claim is neither — it is an ordered STEP in the argument, and its distinctive fields (order, seed provenance, reconciliation links, chapter advancement) belong to no sibling. The spine does not restate the siblings as a second source: each spine claim RECONCILES into the sibling models via `reconciles` links (claim ids from claims_declared.json; big-idea slugs from landing-big-ideas.json) and cites the author's seed statements (`seeds`, the 10-statement draft in book/_design/book-editorial-discipline-directive-260802.md Part A Task 1). Each spine claim: {id, order, statement (<=32 words, split()-counted), seeds[], reconciles: {claims[], big_ideas[]}, reviewed_hash (AS8 freshness seed — the statement hash the chapter labels were reviewed against; a changed statement reddens its advancing chapters until re-reviewed)}. `chapter_advances` maps every outline chapter slug to the spine-claim ids it advances; `chapter_exemptions` marks the chapters whose breadth (or silence) is their job; `claim_exemptions` is the claim-side analogue — genuine premises marked `front-loaded-by-design` (or `bridge`) so they are NOT flagged thin — both with a reason from the closed enums in argument_spine_model.py. The FLAGS are DERIVED by the generator, never authored, informational, and never gate: chapter-side (a non-exempt chapter advancing 0 claims, or more than 3) AND claim-side (a non-exempt claim advanced by 0 chapters or only within Part 0/1 = thin; a claim advanced by more than OVERMAP_CAP chapters = an overmapping-audit surface).

spine.statement: Coding agents make implementation abundant, fast, and cheap — and individually unreliable.
spine.measurand: throughput and cost per change — velocity, per-document cost, refactor wall-clock

spine.statement: Treat a bad output first as evidence about the instructions, representation, task boundary, or environment — not automatically as a fixed capability ceiling.
Human per-change oversight cannot scale with agent throughput; attention must be spent per class of failure, not per change.
spine.measurand: human review effort per change against agent throughput

spine.statement: Ungoverned, the project decays into churn: an increasing share of effort goes to rediscovering context, undoing recent work, and reconciling inconsistencies rather than advancing the system.
spine.measurand: share of effort on rediscovery, undo, and reconciliation versus advancing the system

spine.statement: Churn is a symptom; its causes are exactly three not-knowings — what to build, how to realize it, how to change safely.
Build the environment first: encode each obligation as a mechanism the environment enforces — mechanized, not remembered — so quality is a property of the ground.
spine.measurand: support-apparatus LoC against production LoC — the build-the-environment-first revealed preference

spine.statement: Externalize engineering knowledge and intent into progressively richer representations: selected context, connected knowledge, invariant-bearing models, so commodity intelligence reasons through a compact world and engineers gain a surface to specify and predict.
spine.measurand: agent tokens-to-answer under model navigation; code-to-model coverage

spine.statement: Give engineering intent authority over autonomous work by binding obligations to deterministic mechanisms — constrain, sense, validate, gate; where Modeling makes intent explicit, Alignment makes it binding.
spine.measurand: drift-detection signal quality and reconciliation labor for models and implementation

spine.statement: The theses are causally linked, not parallel: Modeling turns implicit knowledge into representation; Alignment attaches authority; the richer the model, the more obligations move from judgment into enforcement.
Velocity surfaces the unforeseeable failure; the engineer's recurring task converts each recurrence into durable machinery.
spine.measurand: recurrences converted to durable controls; real bugs caught by the model and lint loop

spine.statement: The sync economics changed. Agents sharply reduce the recurring labor of keeping models and implementation reconciled.
spine.measurand: recurring reconciliation labor keeping models and implementation consistent

spine.statement: This makes serious model-based software engineering practical: models can become the working language through which agents reason and engineers specify, predict, and govern.

The engineering lifecycle remains; the allocation of work changes. Agents occupy much of implementation, while human effort concentrates on intent, architecture, model authorship, validation, and judgment.
spine.measurand: allocation of implementation to agents versus human effort on intent, architecture, and validation

spine.statement: The DocAble case grounds the method and motivates hypotheses for broader use — a single-case field report, never a proof.

Each conversion banks engineering capital that lowers the future cost of change, so effort compounds — later work extends capability instead of re-solving settled problems, while that capital stays fit.
spine.measurand: share of future effort extending capability versus re-solving settled problems, as effective conversion coverage grows
